summary: Enterprise AI in 2026 has coalesced around managed model-API aggregators offered by the major cloud providers, which let corporations consume foundation models (GPT, Claude, Llama, Gemini, Mistral, and more) through a single secure API while keeping data inside their existing cloud tenancy. There is no single winner; the best fit is usually dictated by a company's existing cloud footprint, compliance needs, and desired model breadth. AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, and Google Vertex AI dominate adoption, with Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx, Oracle, and Cloudflare serving specific data-gravity and edge niches.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts and responses stay within the company's own cloud VPC/region and are not used to train vendor models, satisfying regulatory and IP-protection requirements.
Compliance and governance: aggregators inherit the cloud provider's certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR) and provide centralized audit logging, guardrails, and access controls.
Single billing and existing contracts: usage rolls into the existing cloud enterprise agreement and committed spend, avoiding new vendor procurement and leveraging negotiated discounts.
Model choice and portability: one API provides access to many models from different labs, reducing lock-in to a single AI vendor and enabling quick switching as models improve.
Native integration and security: unified identity (IAM/Entra), VPC networking, private endpoints, data pipelines, and monitoring already used by the enterprise extend directly to AI workloads.

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token (on-demand) plus Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity; batch and fine-tuning priced separately. Rolls into AWS billing.
key_features: Widest model choice behind one API
platforms.best_for: AWS-centric enterprises wanting the broadest multi-model choice (especially Claude) behind one secure API.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service (Azure AI Foundry)
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token with Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; committed-use discounts via Microsoft enterprise agreements.
key_features: Exclusive enterprise access to OpenAI frontier models
Entra ID (Azure AD) identity and RBAC
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first organizations wanting first-party OpenAI models with enterprise governance.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI (Model Garden)
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token on-demand plus Provisioned Throughput sold in GSUs (Generative AI Scale Units) for reserved capacity (e.g., 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec).
key_features: Native Gemini plus third-party models in Model Garden
VPC Service Controls and private networking
platforms.best_for: Google Cloud / data-analytics-heavy enterprises wanting Gemini plus multimodal (image/video) and MLOps tooling.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits; LLM functions billed per token/credit within existing Snowflake account.
key_features: Models run directly against governed Snowflake data (no data movement)
SQL and Python LLM functions (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE)
platforms.best_for: Enterprises with data already in Snowflake wanting AI directly on governed data with zero data movement.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Subscription plus consumption (Resource Units/tokens); available on IBM Cloud, on-premises, and hybrid/multicloud.
key_features: watsonx.governance for model risk, lineage, and bias monitoring
watsonx Orchestrate for cross-platform agent management
Open-source and IBM Granite model tuning
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises needing hybrid/on-prem deployment, strong governance, and agent orchestration.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity; integrated into OCI and Oracle enterprise agreements.
key_features: Dedicated AI clusters for isolated capacity
Deep integration with Oracle Fusion / Database
platforms.best_for: Oracle database and ERP/Fusion customers wanting AI close to their enterprise applications and data.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-use (neurons/tokens) with a free tier; serverless, no capacity reservation required.
key_features: Serverless inference at the global edge (low latency)
AI Gateway for caching, rate-limiting, logging, and analytics
Integration with Workers, R2, and Vectorize (vector DB)
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, globally distributed, cost-efficient open-model inference at the edge.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs) for model serving, fine-tuning, and training; runs within existing Databricks/cloud account.
key_features: Model Serving with foundation model APIs and external model gateway
Unity Catalog governance and lineage over data and models
platforms.best_for: Data/ML-heavy enterprises building custom and RAG applications on their lakehouse with strong governance.
